exposure: quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) at birth and/or 1 month
IgM-trypomastigote excreted-secreted antigen (TESA) blot at birth and/or 1 month
anti-Trypanosoma cruzi IgG at 6 or 9 months
outcome: accuracy (sensitivity, specificity) of the IgM-SAPA test
cohort: Infants born to Chagas-seropositive mothers were followed for up to 9 months to diagnose congenital Chagas disease.
finding: The IgM-SAPA test showed similar accuracy to qPCR (sensitivity 76.7%-94.3% vs 79.1%-97.1%, specificity 92.6% vs 99.5%) when evaluated at birth, suggesting its potential as an early diagnostic tool for congenital Chagas disease.
